purpose: Resolve the material architecture uncertainty of whether a small, trainable interaction mechanism among the already eligible user_id, video_id, tab, hour, and weekday features is justified after the additive scorer showed strong GAUC but heterogeneous top-five quality in tab slices. Seek evidence on interaction structures that are effective without introducing unavailable or post-impression features.
query: Context-aware recommender ranking literature comparing additive linear categorical models with low-order feature-interaction models (factorization machines, field-aware factorization machines, or compact neural interactions), focusing on user-item-request-context interactions for implicit binary feedback and top-k ranking.

purpose: Resolve whether changing only the training objective is a defensible next experiment for the observed gap between usable within-user GAUC and weaker, context-dependent nDCG@5. The evidence should clarify expected GAUC/nDCG trade-offs, required negative sampling assumptions, and whether an objective change can be evaluated cleanly while preserving the fixed temporal holdout and official metrics.
query: Learning-to-rank objective literature for implicit-feedback recommendation under fixed top-k evaluation, comparing pointwise binary cross-entropy with pairwise ranking losses and listwise/top-k-aware objectives; emphasize effects on per-user AUC versus nDCG@K and practical low-compute training guidance.
